**Manager Dispatching**: The worker manager iterates as long as the global surface is not totally extracted.
It balances the cost between shape quality and distance from the original surface.
A value of $\alpha = 0.4$ is recommended as a good compromise.
This variant refers to the core sequential extension of the tandem algorithm that introduces the component dumping mechanism.
It processes cross-sections sequentially, activating them one by one, simplifying the mesh, and dumping finished components.
The loop runs from $k=1$ to $N-1$ (number of cross-sections), activating cross-section $k$, simplifying with $E_0$, and dumping.
- **Time Complexity**: The parallel version significantly reduces extraction time compared to the sequential tandem algorithm.
- **Memory Complexity**: By dumping completed components and processing blocks, the algorithm minimizes memory consumption.
- **Scalability**: The algorithm scales well with the number of processors, limited primarily by the communication overhead between workers and the manager.
- **Mesh Quality**: The parallel algorithm produces a mesh with equivalent quality (anisotropy variation) to the sequential approach.
